terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation; obruī, to be overwhelmed (by work: opere, negōtiīs)
evidence: Cic. Q. fr. 1.1.4: neque tē obruī tamquam flūctū … sinās (Lewis & Short s.v. contrā)
Traupman 105: to be overwhelmed with work, obruī, tamquam flūctū, sīc opere
terms.comment: Literally “to be covered over”, as by earth or a wave: Cicero’s figure is the wave. Traupman’s obruī, tamquam flūctū, sīc opere is “to be swamped by work as by a wave”.

sources: Lewis & Short: obruo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 105, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
